Definition: a requital, i.e. (secure) retribution, (venal) a fee
BiblicalUsage: Isaiah names the day of the LORD's vengeance the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion, Hosea says the days of recompence have come on Israel, and Micah watches the judge ask for a reward. The same word pays the righteous and bribes the judge, and God tells the difference.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe recompense is the heart of God's justice, because He pays every man according to his work and He is never bought. I hold that the bribes of Micah's day are the warning, and the vengeance of Isaiah's day is the promise.
